terms.plain: A naming word: a person, place, animal, object or idea.
A small word placed before a noun. Spanish articles include el, la, los, las, un and una.
A word used in place of a noun.
A word used to ask for information.
Spanish nouns are grammatically masculine or feminine. This affects articles and adjectives.
Whether a word is singular or plural.
A word that describes a noun and normally agrees with it in gender and number.
terms.example: un gato negro; unas casas blancas

terms.plain: The way related words change form to match gender or number.
terms.example: la gata negra; los gatos negros

terms.plain: A word expressing an action, occurrence or state.
The dictionary form of a verb, usually ending in -ar, -er or -ir.
A verb form commonly used for what happens now or regularly.
Learning through the target language itself, supported by pictures, demonstration, repetition and questions.
terms.example: ¿Qué animal es éste? Éste es un gato.
